messages.subject_clean: Combining summary summary stats from different human genome builds
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Sorry if my question is too basic for this group. But I am really looking for an answer to my below mentioned question i.e. Is it okay to combine summary statistics of different traits which are on the different reference genomes (human genome build hg38 and hg19)?

Thank you in advance.

Best regards,
Rajini

messages.subject: Re: Combining summary summary stats from different human genome builds
messages.subject_clean: Combining summary summary stats from different human genome builds
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajini,

Thanks for following up about this (there are period when these posts get lost in the hectic period of the semester so the lack of response had nothing to do with the question itself as I think it's a great one).

The relevance of the genome builds will likely depend a bit on the level of analysis you are conducting. If you are strictly running genome-wide models, since those only use the LDSC genetic covariance matrices, which are themselves estimated only using common HapMap3 SNPs that are unlikely to shift across builds, I would not anticipate that the build matters. If you are running multivariate GWAS (as it sounds like you are), I would say that it is still not a huge cause for concern as only a small subset of SNPs are likely to both pass QC and listwise deletion that would shift across builds.

With that said, if a software like LDpred is requiring that you use a particular build, or you want to be extra sure that genome builds are not affecting results, there are a number of options out there, but one of the more accessible and easy to use packages that I've found is one in R called MungeSumstats that includes a liftover function that could be used to align all input summary stats to the same build prior to running the sumstats function in Genomic SEM, or to convert the multivariate GWAS summary stats to a particular build. Example code that could be run in R below to convert from build 37 to 38 could be written as:

library(MungeSumstats)

sumstats38 <- MungeSumstats::liftover(sumstats_dt = sumstats37, ref_genome = "GRCh37", convert_ref_genome = "GRCh38", start_col = "BP", end_col = "BP")

Best,
  Andrew

messages.subject: Using genomic SEM in ecology: advice on minimum required sample sizes
messages.subject_clean: Using genomic SEM in ecology: advice on minimum required sample sizes
messages.body_plain:
Dear group,

I was hoping someone could advice me on the possibilities to use genomic SEM beyond human disease and crop breeding. Specifically, I am wondering what minimum sample sizes are recommended to run genomic SEM with adequate power.

The studies I have found to date that use genomic SEM all have the privilege of working with human or plant data that contain over thousands of samples. However, these sample sizes are less common within ecology, although this approach would be of great use to identify genetically correlating traits in our field too. Therefore, I was wondering if there are any rules-of-thumb for conducting genomic SEM with regards to sample size and maximum number of traits one could test with it. Is it of any use to use this approach with sample sizes lower than 1,000?

Many thanks,
Rebecca

messages.subject: Inf values in se - ERROR - generated during SUMSTATS?
messages.subject_clean: Inf values in se - ERROR - generated during SUMSTATS?
messages.body_plain:
For the first time, I ran into this error running the common factor GSEM.

Indeed, I found 187000 plus "Inf" values across the 5 traits in my file generated at Step 3 - sumstats function.

I went back to the underlying trait GWAS files and all SE values were finite (no "Inf" values).

I checked the sumstats file (input for commonFactor function) against underlying trait GWAS - well the first 8 SNPs showing up with se=Inf, and there were finite se's associated with SNPs.  eg.  SNP CHR     BP P         BETA        SE      MAF A1 A2
                      rs6605064   1 812743 1 -0.000723838 0.0107367 0.126726  C  T

So my question - having never run into this before - what has generated Inf values in the Sumstats?  Is there something I can do (other than drop 187000 plus SNPs)?

Thanks in advance.

Daniel (sorry sent from wrong account)
